To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dark current of LWIR Hg0.3Cd0.7Te diodes grown on Si wafrs is 2 orders of magnitude larger than that of similar diodes grown on bulk Cd0.8Zn0.2Te substrates, but that the dark current density of the diodes grown on silicon is comparable to that of diodes grown on CdTe buffer layers.

(i) HgCd Te-on-Si LWIR diode performance is significantly degraded by threading dislocations, (ii) HgCdte-on-Si VLWIR diode performance can be significantly improved with the introduction of a CdSeTe buffer layer, and (iii) the best HgCdTe diode performance on Si is obtained with the use of a CdSe Te buffer layer.
we have successfully grown HgCdTe layers with high quality and low threading dislocation density on CdTe buffer layers grown on Si waf ers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of high-performance LWIR HgCdtTe-on-Si detectors.
the development of high-performance HgCdTe diode arrays grown on Si substrates.
the development of HgCdTet-on-Si technology for LWIR and VLWIR applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we are not quite ready for LWIR HgTe-on-Si, but we are getting close.
the HgCdTE-on-Si technology for the LWIR and VLWIR is still at the very early stage of its development.
the current state-of-the-art for HgCdTe diodes grown on Si is not yet competitive with diodes grown on bulk CdTe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that LWIR diodes can be grown on CdTe/Si substrates.
the HgCdTE-on-Si LWIR diode performance is comparable to that of HgCdTE grown on CdZnTe.

while there is still much room for improvement, the HgCdTE-on-Si technology has made significant progress in recent years, and we are confident that we can extend this progress to the LWIR and VLWIR regimes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of the HgCdTet-on-Si diodes is comparable to that of diodes grown directly on bulk CdZTe substrates.
the performance of HgCdTE diodes grown on Si substrates is comparable to that of diodes grown on bulk CdTe substrates.
the HgCdTE-on-Si approach to LWIR FPAs has the potential for success if the density of dislocations threading through the HgCdte can be reduced to <5E4 cm−2.
